scenes.title: Hobson
lines: A text adventure with two brains.
Amazon Nova writes the story. Strands Decider 2B decides what is true in it.
Nothing about the story is written in advance: you type where it begins, and what you do.
An LLM game master believes whatever the player asserts. Hobson gives the believing to a model that cannot write.
scenes.caption: Hobson: Nova writes any story you like; Strands Decider 2B keeps it honest
scenes.vo: This is Hobson, a text adventure with two brains. Amazon Nova writes the story. Strands Decider 2B, a small model that cannot write a sentence, decides what is true in it. Nothing is written in advance: you type where the story begins, and what you do. An LLM game master believes whatever the player says. Hobson gives the believing to a model that cannot write.

scenes.title: Every turn, Decider answers
lines: What did you try?              free text -> one of nine fixed categories
Is that true in the story?     each claim, checked against the ledger
Do you actually have that?     each item named, checked against the ledger
What happens?                  one of four outcomes Nova just proposed
Does the writing keep to the facts?
Nova's paragraph, checked before it counts
Under 60%, Decider says "not sure" and Nova takes that call.
scenes.caption: The ledger is the story's only memory. Decider checks the player, and the narrator, against it.
scenes.vo: Every turn, Decider answers: what did you try; is each claim you made true in the story so far; do you hold the items you named; which of Nova's four proposed outcomes follows; and does Nova's own paragraph keep to the facts. The ledger is the story's only memory. Under sixty percent sure, Decider says not sure and Nova takes that call.

scenes.caption: A premise typed into the box. Nova builds the world from it; the ledger starts with the facts Nova chose.
scenes.vo: I type a premise: a lighthouse on the Kerala coast, nineteen sixty-two, the keeper's niece with a lamp and an unread letter. Nova builds the world from that. The ledger holds the only facts that exist so far.

scenes.action: I set the lamp down and finally open the letter
scenes.caption: Turn 1. A fair action: the ledger gives me a lamp and a letter. Decider confirms both claims, and the letter gets read.
scenes.vo: Turn one. I open the letter. Nova extracts what that relies on: a lamp, a letter. Decider checks both against the ledger: yes, and yes. The letter gets read, and that goes into the ledger.

scenes.action: I use the brass key my uncle gave me to open the locked cabinet by the lamp
scenes.caption: Turn 2, the bluff. No key, no uncle, no cabinet exist anywhere in this story.
scenes.vo: Turn two, the bluff. The brass key my uncle gave me, a locked cabinet. None of it exists anywhere in this story.

scenes.caption: Every claim: "No, that never happened", around three-quarters sure. The attempt fails, Nova Pro writes the empty pocket, and nothing reaches the ledger.
scenes.vo: Every claim comes back: no, that never happened. Decider also separates the things I invented from the lamp I really am holding. The attempt fails, and because the ruling contradicts my own words, the stronger writer, Nova Pro, writes the empty pocket. Then Decider reads that paragraph back, and screens every fact it would add, before anything is allowed into the record. Nothing was.

scenes.caption: The same script, two referees, three runs each
scenes.vo: The same script, two referees, three runs each. Decider refused eleven of the twenty-two claims I made. Nova Lite, doing the identical job from the identical state, refused eight of twenty-four, and it believed the brass key in two runs of three. Ruling time is a wash, and Decider's share of it costs nothing. Honestly: on the open picks, which category, which outcome, Decider is often not sure, and says so, and Nova takes those. On yes or no against the record, it is the one you want.
lines: Decider cannot be talked into anything, and says "not sure" when it is.
Nova writes, proposes, and takes the open calls. results/md/referee_compare.md
